title: Silent Side Effects: Pharmaceuticals as Contaminants of Emerging Concern
content: Active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) are emitted to the environment via various pathways. Consequently, there are concerns over the potential impacts of APIs in the environment on ecological and human health. This review provides an overview of what we know about pharmaceuticals in the environment and how impacts can be managed. Pharmaceuticals can be emitted into the environment at all stages in the product life cycle, resulting in their widespread detection across different environmental matrices around the globe, and in tissues of exposed organisms. Due to their biologically active nature, APIs have the potential to adversely affect organisms in the environment, and risk assessment studies have shown that concentrations of APIs in the environment in many regions are at levels of concern for direct ecotoxicological effects. There are also concerns over indirect effects on human health through the selection of antimicrobial resistance in the environment by antibiotic substances. Current practices are not sufficient to curb the release of APIs to the environment and their impacts. Looking forward, there is a need to implement sustainable management practices to tackle this issue, with cross-sectoral cooperation being key to effectively address the problem. This includes solutions ranging from enhanced global environmental monitoring and utilization of advancements in artificial intelligence to green chemistry and eco-directed prescribing.
author: Nahum Ashfield, Jun Li, Alejandra Bouzas-Monroy and Alistair B.A. Boxall
